hook: Helen Toner is executive director of Georgetown University's Center for Security and Emerging Technology, where she studies the security implications of AI, export controls, and US-China technology competition. Born and raised in Australia, she holds a BSc in chemical engineering from the University of Melbourne before moving into technology policy, first as a senior research analyst at Open Philanthropy advising on AI grantmaking, then as a research affiliate at Oxford's Centre for the Governance of AI, spending nine months in Beijing studying China's AI ecosystem. In September 2021 she joined OpenAI's board of directors. She left the board in November 2023, after the board's brief removal and reinstatement of CEO Sam Altman, a crisis in which she said the board had been kept in the dark about matters including the launch of ChatGPT and Altman's ownership stake in the OpenAI Startup Fund. She has since testified before multiple congressional committees on AI policy and continues to lead CSET's research program.

timeline.event: Appointed to OpenAI's board of directors
timeline.impact: Joined the board overseeing what would soon become the world's most prominent AI lab, shortly before the launch of ChatGPT.

timeline.event: OpenAI launches ChatGPT without notifying the board in advance
timeline.impact: Toner later said the board learned about the launch on Twitter, an early sign of governance gaps at the company.

timeline.event: OpenAI's board fires and then reinstates CEO Sam Altman, and Toner leaves the board
timeline.impact: Became one of the most closely watched governance failures in AI, prompting broader scrutiny of nonprofit-controlled AI labs.
